topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students, frames the broader cancer biology lecture series, and outlines the specific learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Cellular Mechanisms and Experimental Models of Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cumulative genetic alterations and the breakdown of normal tissue differentiation drive tumor formation and discuss how these processes are modeled in vitro.

topics.label: Tumor Invasion, Metastasis, and Benign versus Malignant Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the transition from localized benign growths to invasive and metastatic malignancies, contrasting their histopathological features and clinical behaviors.

topics.label: Neoplasm Nomenclature and Classification
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes the standard naming conventions and notable exceptions used to classify benign and malignant tumors by their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the anatomical, functional, and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause clinical illness and death.

topics.label: Epidemiology and Comparative Oncology Across Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey the incidence and mortality patterns of major human cancers and compare tumor prevalence across diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Clinical Principles and Organ-Specific Practices of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the rationale for early tumor detection and evaluate the diagnostic methods, efficacy, and trade-offs of screening programs across different organs.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Wrap-Up
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session by referencing the learning outcomes and outlining upcoming practicals and future lectures.
